sections.overview: The Eucla cod is a deepwater gadiform in the family Euclichthyidae. A 2020 revision recognizes it alongside two close relatives, E. microdorsalis and E. robertsi, ending the family’s long treatment as a single-species group.
sections.identification: Two close-set dorsal fins, a raised anal-fin lobe, long pelvic rays and no chin barbel distinguish it from morid cods.
sections.habitat: It inhabits upper continental slopes off Australia and New Zealand, at about 250–800 m in the New Zealand guide.
sections.diet: The available New Zealand guide does not describe specific prey or feeding habits.
sections.behavior: It probably lives near the bottom and is rarely caught in abundance.
sections.reproduction: Its reproductive biology remains poorly known in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: The family revision suggests early juveniles remain pelagic offshore, while adults live close to the seabed; this ontogenetic shift is known from limited available material.
sections.conservation: The taxonomic and identification sources consulted do not give a species-specific global conservation assessment.
